themes_detail.label: Street noise surge
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints surged to 91 THIS WEEK, up 247% from the 8-week baseline of 26.2 weekly complaints (z-score: 4.26), marking the most acute noise crisis in East Harlem in recent months.
evidence: 91 street/sidewalk noise complaints last week vs. 26.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (247% spike, z-score 4.26)
19 vehicle noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 8.0 weekly average (138% spike, z-score 3.67)
Combined street-level noise spikes suggest acute disruption event or seasonal pattern emerging
reporting_angles: Interview residents and businesses on 125th Street and major avenues about noise sources (construction, street vending, vehicles, music venues)
Investigate whether recent development activity (58-62 E. 125th Street rezoning underway) or street events correlate with spike timing

themes_detail.label: Drug activity clustering
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints hit 9 LAST WEEK, up 279% from the 8-week baseline of 2.4 weekly complaints (z-score: 4.2), indicating either a real uptick in street-level drug markets or heightened community reporting of existing activity.
evidence: 9 drug activity complaints last week vs. 2.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (279% spike, z-score 4.2)
Coincides with 14 encampment complaints 2 weeks ago (647% spike, z-score 6.62), suggesting homelessness and substance use may be linked
18 non-emergency police matter complaints 2 weeks ago (227% spike, z-score 5.1) aligns with same timeframe
reporting_angles: Map the geographic concentration of drug activity complaints; interview NYPD about enforcement strategy and resources
Profile the relationship between encampment sites and drug activity reports; connect to mental health and addiction services availability

themes_detail.label: Encampment surge continuing
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints reached 14 two weeks ago, up 647% from the 8-week baseline of 1.9 weekly complaints (z-score: 6.62); while the spike occurred 2 weeks ago, this remains the most statistically extreme deviation in the dataset and suggests an ongoing homelessness crisis.
evidence: 14 encampment complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (647% spike, z-score 6.62—highest z-score in dataset)
Overlaps with spike in non-emergency police matters (18 complaints, 227% up) and drug activity (9 complaints, 279% up) from same period
No recent follow-up data available; unclear if encampments have been cleared or persist
reporting_angles: Ground reporting: locate current encampment sites in CD 111; interview unhoused residents about services and barriers to shelter
City response: DSNY/Parks/NYPD encampment removal protocols; why were 14 reports filed in one week, and what triggered the spike?

themes_detail.label: Litter basket crisis
themes_detail.summary: Litter basket requests exploded to 3 THIS WEEK, up 2300% from the 8-week baseline of 0.1 weekly complaints (z-score: 8.69), the single most extreme spike in the dataset, suggesting either a sudden infrastructure failure or environmental degradation event.
evidence: 3 litter basket requests THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% spike, z-score 8.69—highest z-score in entire dataset)
Unsanitary condition complaints remain elevated across 90-day period (801 total), suggesting chronic sanitation challenges
Community board budget requests for 'Increase Graffiti Removal/Cleaning' indicate long-standing sanitation dissatisfaction
reporting_angles: Investigate: were 3 specific litter baskets removed, damaged, or overflowing? Check DSNY work orders for this week
Broader context: are residents reporting that trash infrastructure is inadequate to serve foot traffic in East Harlem commercial corridors (125th Street area)?

themes_detail.label: Animal-in-park complaints spike
themes_detail.summary: Animal-in-park complaints reached 4 LAST WEEK, up 357% from the 8-week baseline of 0.9 weekly complaints (z-score: 4.0), suggesting either an increase in stray or feral animal populations in East Harlem parks or heightened community concern.
evidence: 4 animal-in-park complaints last week vs. 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (357% spike, z-score 4.0)
Community board budget requests for 'park, building, or access improvements' indicate ongoing parks maintenance concerns
No details available on animal types (rats, dogs, coyotes, etc.) or specific parks affected
reporting_angles: Contact Parks Dept and Animal Care & Control: what animals were reported, at which parks, and what was the response?
Check if spike correlates with seasonal factors (spring migration, breeding season) or reflects degraded park maintenance conditions
